knowledge_tree.title: English for Senior High School (Compulsory 1)
knowledge_tree.content: Comprehensive English language learning for first-year senior high students, covering listening, speaking, reading, writing, and cultural awareness.

children.title: Welcome Unit
children.content: Introduction to senior high school life, making introductions, and describing feelings.

children.title: Making Introductions
children.content: Learn formal and informal ways to introduce oneself and others.

children.title: Formal Introductions
children.content: Using phrases like 'May I introduce...' in formal settings.

children.title: Informal Greetings
children.content: Casual greetings such as 'What's up?' and 'How's it going?'.

children.title: Describing Feelings
children.content: Vocabulary for emotions: anxious, annoyed, frightened, confident, etc.

children.title: Pronunciation: Vowel Sounds
children.content: Practice pronunciation of vowels A, E, I, O, U in different words.

children.title: Unit 1: Teenage Life
children.content: Exploring school life, extra-curricular activities, and teenage challenges.

children.title: School Clubs
children.content: Types of clubs: Ballet, Nature, Volunteer, Debate, etc.

children.title: Club Activities
children.content: What students do in each club, e.g., grow plants in Nature Club.

children.title: The Freshman Challenge
children.content: Adapting to senior high school, choosing courses, and joining activities.

children.title: Course Selection
children.content: How to choose suitable courses with an adviser's help.

children.title: Dealing with Setbacks
children.content: Handling failure, e.g., not making a sports team, and not giving up.

children.title: Learning Strategies
children.content: Methods for effective learning: group work, note-taking, using dictionaries.

children.title: Writing a Student Profile
children.content: Structure and content of a student profile, including personality and hobbies.

children.title: Unit 2: Travelling Around
children.content: Planning trips, making reservations, and exploring different cultures.

children.title: Travel Preparations
children.content: Steps to prepare for a trip: passport, visa, booking tickets and hotels.

children.title: Essential Documents
children.content: Importance of passport and visa for international travel.

children.title: Booking Accommodation
children.content: How to book a hotel room, including special requests.

children.title: Reading a Brochure
children.content: Understanding travel brochures, e.g., about Peru.

children.title: Types of Tours
children.content: Different tours: Machu Picchu, Amazon Rainforest, etc.

children.title: Present Continuous for Future Plans
children.content: Using present continuous tense to talk about future arrangements.

children.title: Writing a Travel Plan
children.content: How to write an email about a travel plan, including destinations and activities.

children.title: Unit 3: Sports and Fitness
children.content: Learning about sports events, athletes, and healthy living.

children.title: Sports Events
children.content: Types of events: soccer games, marathons, boxing matches.

children.title: Living Legends of Sports
children.content: Profiles of athletes like Lang Ping and Michael Jordan.

children.title: Lang Ping's Achievements
children.content: Her role as player and coach, and her determination.

children.title: Michael Jordan's Success
children.content: His skills and mental strength, and his philosophy on failure.

children.title: Tag Questions
children.content: Formation and use of tag questions in conversations.

children.title: Writing a Wellness Page
children.content: Sharing personal changes for better health and fitness.

children.title: Unit 4: Natural Disasters
children.content: Understanding natural disasters, safety measures, and report writing.

children.title: Types of Disasters
children.content: Earthquakes, tornadoes, tsunamis, floods, etc.

children.title: The Tangshan Earthquake
children.content: Description of the 1976 earthquake, its impact, and recovery.

children.title: Warning Signs
children.content: Strange phenomena before the earthquake, e.g., well water changes.

children.title: Aftermath and Revival
children.content: How the city recovered with government and people's efforts.

children.title: Restrictive Relative Clauses
children.content: Using that, which, who, whose, whom to add information about nouns.

children.title: Writing a Summary
children.content: How to summarize a news report about a disaster.

children.title: Unit 5: Languages Around the World
children.content: Exploring language diversity, learning strategies, and the Chinese writing system.

children.title: Diversity of Languages
children.content: Number of languages globally, official UN languages.

children.title: The Chinese Writing System
children.content: History and development of Chinese characters from ancient times.

children.title: Oracle Bone Script
children.content: Early symbols carved on bones and shells.

children.title: Unification under Qinshihuang
children.content: Standardization of characters during the Qin Dynasty.

children.title: Chinese Calligraphy
children.content: Art form based on Chinese characters.

children.title: Language Learning Challenges
children.content: Common problems: listening, politeness, vocabulary.

children.title: Restrictive Relative Clauses with Adverbs
children.content: Using where, when, why in relative clauses.

children.title: Writing a Blog Post
children.content: Sharing language learning experiences and advice.
